title.narrative: Världsbankens Palestinska fond för återuppbyggnad och utveckling
World Bank Palestinian Fund for Reconstruction and Development

description.narrative:
The World Bank Palestinian Fund for Reconstruction and Development Multi-donor Trust Fund (PFRD)’s objective is to strengthen sustainable recovery and reconstruction, economic recovery, and social resilience in West Bank and Gaza through:
1. Macro-fiscal Stability and Public Financial Management 2. Human Capital Investment and Service Delivery (including Infrastructure) 3. Private Sector Development and Job Generation 4. Protection to the Poor and at-risk Population, and 5. Gaza Recovery and Reconstruction.

Världsbankens palestinska fond för återuppbyggnad och utveckling (PFRD) har som mål att stärka hållbar återhämtning och återuppbyggnad, ekonomisk återhämtning och social motståndskraft på Västbanken och i Gaza genom:
1. Makroekonomisk stabilitet och offentlig finansförvaltning. 2. Investeringar i humankapital och tillhandahållande av tjänster (inklusive infrastruktur). 3. Utveckling av den privata sektorn och skapande av arbetstillfällen. 4. Skydd av fattiga och utsatta befolkningsgrupper. 5. Återhämtning och återuppbyggnad av Gaza.

The objective of the PFRD is to strengthen sustainable recovery and reconstruction, economic reform, and social resilience in the West Bank and Gaza.
The activities to be financed by the Trust Fund are:
Bank-executed activities
(a) Strengthening sustainable recovery and reconstruction, economic reform and social resilience. (i) provision of technical assistance to support a stable macro-fiscal framework; (ii) provision of technical assistance to improve human capital and service delivery; (iii) provision of technical assistance to promote financial and private sector development and job generation; (iv) provision of technical assistance to strengthen social protection to the poor and at-risk population and (v) Provision of technical assistance to support recovery and reconstruction in Gaza.
b) Implementation support. Carrying out of identification and appraisal of, and provision of implementation support to and supervision of Recipient-executed activities.
(c) Program management and administration activities for the Trust Fund, including but not limited to, supporting any program governance arrangements and Trust Fund related meetings; planning and executing work plans and budgets; managing communication and conducting outreach; disseminating lessons learned; reporting on progress; and monitoring and evaluating the program.
Recipient-executed activities
(I) Macro-fiscal stability and public financial management. (i) improving public financial management and procurement systems of the Palestinian Authority; (ii) supporting Palestinian institutions in technological improvements and digital modernization to better deliver and engage with the Palestinian people; (iii) improving fiscal sustainability efforts; and (iv) providing budget support.
(II) Human Capital and Service delivery. (i) supporting energy, water, urban development, climate, digital infrastructure and digital skills development with a lens to address gender gaps in digital access, usage and literacy; (ii) supporting good governance and rationalization of health expenditures; and (iii) supporting key areas for human capital improvement, including service delivery in education and health, especially for early childhood development and improved employability.
(III) Financial and Private Sector Development and Job Generation.(i) enhancing entrepreneurship and innovation, investment climate, trade, industry interventions, SME access to finance, and industry-driven human capital improvement (especially for youth and women); (ii) supporting private sector capital mobilization through deployment of a range of financing instruments aimed at de-risking investors and creating jobs; and (ii) supporting COVID-19 related relief, recovery and growth of the Palestinian private sector.
(IV) Social protection to the Poor and at-risk Population. (i) Strengthening social protection (i.e., adaptive social safety nets that include institutionalization of the case management system) and resiliency to shock; (ii) Supporting economic empowerment and job generation, including deployment of cash transfer and cash for work activities that combines communications and behavioral tools to reduce family stress and prevent domestic violence; and (iii) supporting resiliency to as well as relief and recovery from crisis.
(V) Gaza Recovery and Reconstruction. Activities will align with results from technical assistance, including the Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment and the Conflict Recovery Framework. These activities will involve immediate to long-term recovery initiatives and include, but are not limited to: (i) Supporting recovery and reconstruction needs in Gaza, particularly the rehabilitation of essential services, (ii) Promoting economic, social, and environmental sustainability, (iii) Fostering private sector job creation and strengthening the financial sector, and (iv) Prioritizing investment in the education and health sectors.
